title: Cohort-aware Quality Lighthouse with Sliding-score Gating for Staged Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a reliable, low-noise system to detect meaningful quality regressions during canary / A/B / shadow rollouts without producing frequent false positives from distributional skews. Current golden-prompt gates are effective for single global thresholds but struggle with heterogeneous customer cohorts and traffic characteristics (prompt length, domain, language).

Proposal: Build a 'Quality Lighthouse' service that computes cohort-aware score baselines and applies sliding-score gating with hysteresis for staged model promotions. Key ideas: 1) Cohort baselining: maintain per-customer and per-cohort historical score distributions for our canonical eval sets (golden prompts + operational probes). 2) Sliding windows & hysteresis: use short (5-30m) and medium (1-6h) windows to detect transient blips vs sustained regressions; require sustained deviation across both windows before action. 3) Score bucketing: compute distributional shift by bucketing prompt-level scores (pass/fail, near-miss bands) rather than only mean delta; this reduces sensitivity to outliers. 4) Context-aware weighting: reweight eval probes by observed traffic similarity (length, language, domain) to the live traffic during the rollout. 5) Risk budgets: allow per-customer/tenant risk budgets that tolerate small localized deltas and auto-quarantine only when budget is exceeded. 6) Auto-action choreography: when thresholds breach, orchestrate graduated actions: a) elevate sampling for the affected cohort, b) divert that cohort to shadow/quarantine, c) initiate rollback if breaches persist after cooldown.

What this changes: - New Quality Lighthouse microservice with an API to register probe sets, report live scores, and subscribe to gating events. - Runtime integration: canary orchestrator will call the Lighthouse to determine per-cohort gating decisions and to log events to Console. - Console: new per-cohort histogram and two-window timeline visualization for easy triage. - Eval infra: add lightweight per-probe metadata (expected token length distribution, domain tags) used for reweighting.

Acceptance criteria: - Detects injected 6% absolute degradation on a target cohort in staged canary tests within 30 minutes and triggers an auto-quarantine after confirmation on the 1-hour window. - Maintains <2 false-positive auto-quarantines per month across all canaries in integration tests (measured on replayed production traffic). - Console shows per-cohort bucketed histograms and sliding window overlays for every rollout. - API for probe registration and gating decisions documented and used by canary orchestrator.

Open questions / trade-offs: - Sensitivity vs signal noise: tighter thresholds reduce risk but increase alert noise; we'll expose configurable sensitivity per project. - Statefulness cost: maintaining per-customer baselines increases storage/compute; we'll prune baselines for low-traffic tenants and use sketching for long tails. - Privacy/PII: baseline storage uses only anonymized probe identifiers and aggregated score buckets; confirm with security.

Implementation milestones: 1) Spec + schema for probe metadata (2w) 2) Lighthouse prototype: ingestion + two-window aggregator + simple gating (3w) 3) Integrate with canary orchestrator + Console visuals (2w) 4) Small-scale canary run on internal customers (2w) 5) Iterate thresholds and expand to public rollouts (ongoing).

Links: Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RO/pages/QL-Spec, Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/7812, Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/quality-lighthouse
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial spec posted to Confluence. Called out need for per-cohort baselines and two-window hysteresis. Requested early input from PM and Observability teams.

2026-02-18 - Diego Morales: Pushed prototype ingestion + bucketed scoring into a feature branch. Noted that naive mean-delta flagged long-prompt mix changes as regressions; switched to length-aware reweighting in the branch.
2026-02-22 - Priya Kaur (PM): Reviewed spec; requested per-tenant risk budget UI and tighter audit logging for compliance. Suggested a default conservative sensitivity for first 60d.
2026-03-01 - Observability (review): Recommended using quantile sketches for long-tail baseline retention. Called out costs; suggested sample-based pruning for tenants with <100 daily probes.

2026-03-04 - Diego Morales: Ran internal replay test (week-of-traffic) against prototype. Observed a false-positive when customer A switched to longer prompts; adjusted reweighting to account for median length alignment. New results: false positives reduced by ~60% in replay.

2026-03-08 - Security review (comment): Confirmed aggregated score buckets acceptable but asked for explicit KMS policy for any exported artifacts. Marked security_review_required=false until we export raw traces.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria and milestone dates; created PR for the Lighthouse schema and added integration ticket for Console visuals (PM-2104). Next: dogfood on internal Dedicated cluster this month.
notes: Prototype uses 2-window confirmation and bucketed delta. We should run A/B with a conservative default and surface a rollback rationale in Console event logs.
